name: Chloe Bennett
presenting_complaint: Right iliac fossa pain for 18 hours

medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (occasionally missed doses)
medical_history.social: University student. Sexually active, one partner, inconsistent contraception. Non-smoker, social alcohol.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: Chloe Bennett, a 22-year-old woman, presents with an 18-hour history of right iliac fossa pain, now sharp and worsening, with one episode of vomiting and low-grade fever. She is sexually active with inconsistent contraception. HR 96, temp 37.6, BP 112/70. She looks uncomfortable and guards the right iliac fossa.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: SOCRATES of pain: onset, migration (periumbilical to RIF suggests appendicitis), constant vs colicky, severity, aggravating/relieving
Gynaecological/obstetric history: LMP, cycle regularity, chance of pregnancy, contraception use and adherence
Sexual history and STI risk; prior ectopic, PID, or pelvic surgery; vaginal discharge or abnormal bleeding
Associated symptoms: nausea/vomiting, anorexia, fever, urinary symptoms, bowel habit change
Red-flag screen: syncope, shoulder-tip pain, significant vaginal bleeding (suggesting ruptured ectopic)
Explicitly ask about possibility of pregnancy and document
objective: Abdominal exam: RIF tenderness, guarding, rebound/percussion tenderness, Rovsing/psoas/obturator signs
Vital signs and assessment for haemodynamic instability (concealed ectopic haemorrhage)
Point-of-care urine beta-hCG performed and documented BEFORE any imaging
Bimanual/speculum pelvic examination for cervical motion tenderness, adnexal mass/tenderness, discharge
Temperature and signs of peritonism; urinalysis for infection/blood
Pelvic/transvaginal ultrasound as first-line imaging (arrange after pregnancy status known)
assessment: Acute appendicitis as a leading differential in right iliac fossa pain
Must-exclude gynaecological emergencies: ruptured ectopic pregnancy and ovarian torsion
Wider differential: pelvic inflammatory disease, ruptured/haemorrhagic ovarian cyst, ureteric colic, urinary tract infection, mesenteric adenitis
plan: Urine (and serum if positive) beta-hCG FIRST - documented before any imaging is ordered
IV access, IV fluids if unwell, IV analgesia (e.g. paracetamol 1g IV +/- fentanyl 25-50 microg IV titrated) and antiemetic (ondansetron 4mg IV)
Bloods: FBC, CRP, UEC, beta-hCG, group and hold; MSU and urinalysis
Pelvic/transvaginal ultrasound as first imaging; reserve CT for diagnostic uncertainty AND pregnancy excluded
Keep nil by mouth pending surgical review
Refer surgical registrar for suspected appendicitis; refer gynaecology URGENTLY if pregnancy positive or ectopic/torsion suspected
If positive hCG with empty uterus and any instability - treat as resuscitation and theatre call, escalate immediately

critical_errors: Ordering imaging (ultrasound/CT) before performing and documenting a pregnancy test (beta-hCG) - the pregnancy test comes first, every time
Failing to consider ectopic pregnancy or ovarian torsion in a woman of reproductive age with RIF pain
Giving CT with ionising radiation to a potentially pregnant woman without first excluding pregnancy
must_not_miss: Beta-hCG performed and documented before imaging
